WORKDIR /app
ENV PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 ENV PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1

# Algorithmic Amplification of Gender Discourses: Hypergamy Engagement Benchmark
![Python Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.11.9-blue.svg) ![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg) ![Docker Ready](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-Ready-brightgreen.svg)
## Title & Project Overview * **Repository Name:** `hypergamy-engagement` * **Author:** Yertis Ydyrys * **GitHub Link:** [https://github.com/yertisydyrys-jpg/hypergamy-engagement.git](https://github.com/yertisydyrys-jpg/hypergamy-engagement.git)
This research project presents an automated empirical pipeline designed to evaluate algorithmic amplification and user engagement dynamics ($\text{ER}$) across major social media platforms (**TikTok**, **Instagram Reels**, and **YouTube Long-form**). Focusing on gender and relationship discourses in 2026, the pipeline measures statistically significant differences in user engagement using standardized log-transformed metrics.
---
## Research Question (RQ) * **RQ1 (Qualitative/NLP):** What dominant narrative triggers and sentiment patterns characterize viral hypergamy content? * **RQ2 (Quantitative Core):** How do recommendation feed architectures (short-form algorithmic feeds vs. long-form content) influence user engagement rate ($\log(\text{ER})$) for hypergamy discourse?
---
## Planned Benchmark Metrics
| Metric | Type | Target Threshold / Target Range | Purpose | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | $\log(\text{ER}_{\text{view}})$ | Primary | Continuous $[-\infty, 0]$ | Core statistical metric for cross-platform comparison | | Welch's $F$-Statistic | Statistical | $p < 0.05$ ($\alpha = 0.05$) | Test hypothesis $H_1$ vs. $H_0$ | | Eta-squared ($\eta^2$) | Effect Size | $> 0.06$ (Medium effect) | Quantify practical significance | | Data Completeness | Guardrail | $\ge 95\%$ valid records | Prevent data distortion | | Cohen's $\kappa$ | Guardrail | $\ge 0.70$ inter-rater reliability | Human annotation validity |
---
## Repository Structure
```text hypergamy-engagement/ ├── README.md # Project overview and quickstart ├── LICENSE # MIT License ├── .gitignore # Git exclusion rules ├── Dockerfile # Reproducible Docker container config ├── requirements.txt # Strictly pinned dependencies ├── configs/ │ └── config.yaml # Experiment parameters ├── data/ │ └── sample/ │ └── sample.csv # Micro test dataset (10 rows) ├── src/ │ └── main.py # Executable benchmark script ├── docs/ │ └── METHODOLOGY_PASSPORT.md # Methodology card └── results/ └── log.txt # Generated output log

## Quickstart Guide
### Option A: Using Docker (Recommended for Reproducibility)
```bash # 1. Build the Docker image docker build -t hypergamy-benchmark .
# 2. Run the benchmark pipeline docker run --rm hypergamy-benchmark ```
### Option B: Local Python Environment
```bash # 1. Install exact dependencies pip install -r requirements.txt
# 2. Execute benchmark pipeline python src/main.py ```
Expected output will be printed to stdout and saved to `results/log.txt`.
